newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Wind blows down Swiss cable cars, no-one hurt.
newsitem.headline: Wind blows down Swiss cable cars, no-one hurt.

text.p: Strong winds knocked three empty cable-cars to the ground and trapped around 50 people in other gondolas on the same line in the Swiss Alpine resort of Zermatt, authorities said on Thursday.
Rescuers managed to bring down all the passengers by ropes with no injuries in about an hour and a half.
The ski lift had already been forced to halt when a sudden gust knocked the main cable on the empty, downhill side out of its rollers.
Three of the four-person cabins on the downhill cable fell to the ground, said Josef Burgener, director of the Zermatter Rothornbahn lift company that operates the Blauhard line which was hit.
Between 44 and 50 people were trapped in the gondolas, which were going uphill to a ski area across from the Matterhorn mountain that towers over Zermatt.
Those people had to be brought down by ropes from the cabins because it was too windy for a helicopter rescue, Burgener said.
